title: What If You Never Slept Again?

scenes.text: What if you never slept again? Day one feels fine. It isn't.
After twenty-four hours your reactions match someone legally drunk.
By day two your brain starts taking microsleeps: seconds of sleep with your eyes open.
By day three, hallucinations. Shadows move. Voices that aren't there.
The record is eleven days, set by a seventeen-year-old in nineteen sixty-four. He recovered.
But a rare disease that switches sleep off completely is fatal within months. Sleep isn't rest. It's maintenance.

description:
What if you never slept again?
One day: drunk-level reactions. Two: microsleeps. Three: hallucinations. The record is 11 days; a disease that removes sleep entirely is fatal.
What should we run through next?
